queries.hook: I feel jealous of someone close to me. Inside, something doesn't sit right and I can't name it, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: Comparison and envy burn at another's success; measuring your life against theirs steals the contentment in your own.
queries.steady: Your own path, walked imperfectly, is better than another's walked well; what is yours is enough to begin with.
queries.act: Walk your own path, even imperfectly, rather than someone else's well; be grateful for what is yours and rejoice in others' good.
queries.story: A story of a seeker whose mind will not settle, facing measuring yourself against others.

plan_v3.first_line: You feel betrayed by your own heart for resenting the very person you love.

hook.speaker: Bharata
hook.setting: Grieving Kausalya accuses Bharata of plotting Ram's exile; he knew nothing of it.
hook.sanskrit: आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकल्मषम्। विपुलां च मम प्रीतिं स्थितां जानासि राघवे॥
hook.line: Why blame me, who knew nothing? You know what I feel for him.
hook.translation: Noble lady, why do you blame me, who knew nothing and did nothing wrong? You know how deep my love for Ram is.
hook.why: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.

prasang.title: Bharata wrongly blamed
prasang.summary: Bharata turns on his mother in fury. Then Ram's grieving mother assumes he plotted it all, and her words cut him like a needle in a wound. He falls at her feet and swears his innocence until she believes him.
prasang.story_hook: He had done nothing, and the one person whose good opinion he needed was sure he had done it all.
prasang.lesson: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.

alternates.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
alternates.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
alternates.sanskrit: अरणीमग्निकामो वा मथ्नाति दहृयं मम / वाचा दुरुक्तं देवर्षे तन्मां दहति नित्यदा
alternates.line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
alternates.translation: My heart is churned the way someone wanting fire churns a fire-stick. The harsh words my relatives say keep burning me, day after day.
alternates.why: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

prasang.title: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron
prasang.summary: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
prasang.story_hook: Krishna, who guided a war, admitted to a sage that he could not keep the peace in his own family.
prasang.lesson: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.
